results.content: # Types of Record Linkage¶. There are two main types of record linkage - Deterministic and Probabilistic. ## Deterministic Linkage¶. Deterministic Linkage is a **rules-based** approach for joining records together. In general, Deterministic linkage is:. While Splink is primarily a tool for Probabilistic linkage, Deterministic linkage is also supported (utilising blocking rules). See the example notebooks to see how this is Deterministic linkage is implemented in Splink. ## Probabilistic Linkage¶. Probabilistic Linkage is a **evidence-based** approach for joining records together. Linkage is probabilistic in the sense that it relies on the balance of evidence. In a large dataset, observing that two records match on the full name 'Robert Smith' provides some evidence that these two records may refer to the same person, but this evidence is inconclusive. However, the cumulative evidence from across multiple features within the dataset (e.g. date of birth, home address, email address) can provide conclusive evidence of a match. The evidence for a match is commonly represented as a probability. For example, putting the first 2 records of the table above through a probabilistic model gives a an overall probability that the records are a match:. Given these probabilities, unlike (binary) Deterministic linkage, the user can choose an **evidence threshold** for what they consider a match before creating a new unique identifier. This is important, as it allows the linkage to be customised to best support the specific use case. * minimise False Positive matches (i.e. where False Negatives are less of a concern), a higher threshold for a match can be chosen. * maximise True Positive matches (i.e. where False Positives are less of a concern), a lower threshold can be chosen. For a more in-depth introduction to Probabilistic Data Linkage, including an interactive version of the waterfall chart above, see Robin Linacre's Blog. Splink is primarily a tool for Probabilistic linkage, and implements the Fellegi-Sunter model - the most common probabilistic record linkage model. See the Splink Tutorial for a step by step guide for Probabilistic linkage in Splink.

results.title: A hybrid approach to record linkage using a combination of deterministic and probabilistic methodology
results.content: Deterministic linkage methods, when performed independently, yielded 4505 linked pairs (consisting of 2 records linked together within or across data sources). However, the fragmented US healthcare system and the nonexistence of a universal patient identifier across systems necessitates accurate record linkage (RL) solutions.1,2 Individual-level health data are often scattered across disparate healthcare systems, particularly for individuals with complex chronic conditions.3 Without a universal unique patient identifier, RL is accomplished using personally identifiable information (PII) such as first name, last name, date of birth, and social security number.4,5 However, variable patterns of data quality and missingness in PII between data sources may impact RL performance.6. More advanced deterministic methods enable approximate matching by comparing encoded data (eg, SOUNDEX) instead of original linkage variable values or fuzzy matching algorithms.9,10 Probabilistic methods are computationally more complex but perform well even in the presence of missing or erroneous RL data values.11,12 The most widely used probabilistic RL technique is the Fellegi–Sunter method which calculates the likelihood of a match/nonmatch outcome based on the weighted agreement of each linkage variable.13,14 Probabilistic methods generate a normalized continuous match score ranging from 0 (nothing in common) to 100 (all linkage variables match exactly). Preference for using deterministic versus probabilistic linkage methods depend largely on factors such as quality of linkage data (eg, presence of erroneous or missing data), performance priority (precision, recall, and F-measure), and linkage efficiency (runtime).11,12,15,16 Differences in linkage performance between the 2 methods diminish as the size of the data set increases, and if combined, allows researchers to leverage the advantages of each method.17 We describe the implementation and evaluation of a hybrid RL method that improved linkage accuracy in a statewide surveillance system of a rare chronic disease: the Colorado Congenital Heart Disease (COCHD) Surveillance System. Therefore, data normalization is typically performed on linkage variables such as first name, last name, date of birth, address, phone number, and social security number (SSN).19–25 Duplicate records will likely exist in each data source and will be detected in the final linkage results. In this population-based congenital heart disease surveillance system, we have shown that, when performing RL and de-duplication of individuals within and across disparate data sources, a hybrid RL routine outperformed independent deterministic and probabilistic linkage methods.

results.title: What is the difference between deterministic and probabilistic identity data?
results.content: # WTF is the difference between deterministic and probabilistic identity data? In the case of ad tech, probabilistic data can be used to create an identifier. **How is deterministic data used for advertising identity?**Deterministic identifiers use deterministic data to assign identity to a person online or using a mobile device in order to track that identified person across websites or apps for ad targeting or measurement. **So how is deterministic data used to assign identity?**Deterministic identity is achieved when an email address supplied by a publisher or advertiser is matched to the same email address in an identity graph or database of logged-in users. Very often ad tech systems can’t match identities because someone is not logged in or an email address or other piece of deterministic data is not available. When publishers want to assign identity to someone who is not logged in, or a demand-side platform or identity graph provider wants to figure out if there’s a match between a site visitor and another existing ID, they employ probabilistic methods to assign identity based on a variety of probabilistic data points. **Do companies communicate whether an identity has been assigned based on deterministic or probabilistic data?**. While identity tech firms provide information about how they create or link IDs in technical documentation and materials provided to clients, their IDs themselves don’t reveal whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used. **What types of information is used to assign probabilistic identity?**Some identity tech firms call the information used to piece together probabilistic identity “soft signals” or “non-unique device characteristics.” Typical data points used include IP address, timestamps, browser version or screen resolution. **Um, isn’t this just fingerprinting?**Fingerprinting also triangulates a variety of data points to establish identity, but ad and identity tech execs often stress that there are distinctions between the two. For example, some identity tech firms argue that fingerprinting usually happens mainly on the advertiser side, when advertisers or ad tech firms want to create persistent identifiers without the knowledge or approval of people or publishers. “Most ad tech companies, most identity solutions, the probabilistic IDs, these are based on fingerprinting technology — but they’re not calling it fingerprinting.”.
